text:
alex: quick heads-up — I ran a perf pass on the branch that splits prefill and decode into soft-isolated lanes. results are interesting, wanted to surface before i push more changes.

maria: nice, short summary pls? numbers and how you measured. :eyes:

alex: short: p50 similar, p95 improved ~8%, p99 improved ~12% for bursty short prompts, but we see decode-tail spikes for long streaming sessions (p999 up ~30ms). measurement: 1h synthetic trace (50k reqs) using local devbench + kv-warmup on the same host.

jamal: do you have the profiler flame or kernel selection traces? curious if kernel fallback is causing tail.

alex: yes — attaching small excerpt inline:

```
# sample trace (filtered)
prefill-lane: avg-kernel=matmul_q8_fast, mean-token-ms=0.9
decode-lane: avg-kernel=matmul_q8_fallback, mean-token-ms=1.8
kv-hit-rate (prefill): 92%
kv-hit-rate (decode): 74% (decodes often miss because we split lanes)
```

pat: hmm kv hit drop on decode explains tail. splitting helped scheduling but lost cache locality. any ideas for improving decode cache priming?

alex: thinking of two heuristics: 1) soft reservoir tokens: each request reserves small token-budget on decode lane if prefill KV says it will likely continue, to keep replica hot. 2) micro-join window: allow decode to steal prefill's kernel affinity for first N tokens to reduce fallback.

maria: can we express that as queue policy? like "reserve X tokens per request" and "allow N-second affinity affinity window"?

jamal: yes — queue policy sounds right. proposed config snippet that I ran locally:

```
queue_policy: {
  decode_reservation_tokens: 8,
  affinity_window_ms: 40,
  allow_affinity_steal: true,
  kernel_hinting: "prefer-hot-kernel-first"
}
```

pat: how did that run?

jamal: small run: decode kv-hit -> 86% (up from 74), p99 improved ~9ms, p999 reduced ~12ms on streams. but we saw a small throughput regression (~1.6%) when noisey concurrent prefill spikes happen.

alex: that throughput hit likely due to reservations reducing packing efficiency. tradeoff is predictable tail vs raw throughput. i sketched an adaptive mode where reservation tokens scale based on recent kv-hit rate and batch fill ratio.

maria: nice. can you add a very short pseudo algorithm for the adaptive scaling?

alex: sure —

```
// every 500ms window
if (kv_hit_rate_decode < 0.8 && batch_fill < 0.85) {
  reserve_tokens = clamp(reserve_tokens + 2, 0, 16)
} else if (kv_hit_rate_decode > 0.9 || batch_fill > 0.95) {
  reserve_tokens = max(reserve_tokens - 1, 0)
}
```

pat: we should also consider jittering the enqueue delay so decode batches don't align and thrash kernels. small random delay (2-8ms) before enqueue could smooth bin-packing.

jamal: agree. also we need to update kernel-selection to prefer fast-quant kernels if runway tokens reserved > threshold, to avoid fallback during steal. that's a simple hint to runtime.

ci-bot: perf-check: branch prefill-decode-lane-reservoir shows +0.3% overall latency improvement on ci microbench, regression on throughput -1.7% (non-blocking).

maria: next steps: (1) add adaptive reservation prototype in scheduler (2) add jittered enqueue option (3) add kernel-hint plumbing so queues can bias kernel selection (4) run 24h mixed-workload job and collect traces.

alex: i'll PR the scheduler changes today, will include a small benchmark harness. tagging @jamal for kernel-hint review when it's ready.

jamal: ack — i'll look at kernel plumbing. flag: need to ensure hints don't violate multi-tenant constraints (no hard pinning).

pat: +1. let's also add a small eval to measure semantic delta (to ensure quality unaffected) — maybe run our prompt-set against the decode-lane fallback path.

alex: yup will add. thanks all :rocket:
